Senator lngwersen, Representative Meyer and members of the Joint Committee on Health and Human Services, my name is Kara Hay, and I am the President and Chief Executive Officer for Penquis, Maine's largest Community Action Agency. l am also a long-time resident of Penobscot County and a mother to my amazing son Sam. Thank
you for the opportunity to provide written testimony in support of LD 1061.
Known formally as the Maine Child Abuse & Neglect Prevention Councils, the purpose of the Maine Prevention
Councils is to encourage and maintain coordinated community efforts in each county to prevent child abuse and neglect through the provision of family-strengthening programs.

Two of Maine's Prevention Councils have been embedded within and led by Penquis for over 20 years. Both the Penobscot and Piscataquis Prevention Council encourage and coordinate community efforts to prevent child
abuse from occurring. Penquis's Prevention Councils provide a trusted, non-stigmatizing place for all parents and
caregivers to receive the support all parents need from time to time.

Our Prevention services include public awareness activities, evidenced based parent education, child safety education, training for professionals, referrals to services and concrete support for families. Our Prevention Councils are committed to implementing data-informed strategies to meet the needs of our community and
deliver evidence-based prevention strategies that work.

Every community benefits from having a local entity that is focused on creating spaces and services that build relationships and have knowledge about resources that are available. The Prevention Councils are that place that community members and families can go to for support without judgement.

LD 1061 proposes to support the critical and statutory role the Maine Prevention Councils have as the primary community entity to coordinate and provide strategic support and services to prevent child abuse and neglect locally. This legislation would increase our capacity to provide universal community support for families to

promote child safety and family well-being.

Testimony of Melissa Hackett Coordinator, Maine Child Welfare Action Network
in support of LD 1061, An Act to Increase Community Support for Families in Maine
April 4, 2025
Senator lngwersen, Representative Meyer, and esteemed members of the Health and
Human Services Committee. My name is Melissa Hackett. i am a policy associate with
Maine Children's Alliance and serve as the coordinator for the Maine Child Welfare Action
Network. i am offering testimony today in support of LD 1061.
The purpose of the statewide Maine Child Abuse Prevention Councils is to encourage and maintain coordinated community efforts in each county to prevent child abuse and neglect through family-strengthening programs. The Prevention Councils are each county's primary community organizations providing services and coordinating community efforts to prevent child abuse by strengthening families. Services can include public awareness activities, child safety education, parent education, support and information for parents, referral to services, and training for professionals.
Despite this important role, the Prevention Councils have not been funded across the board at a level that ensures they have the capacity to be that community go-to resource
for families looking for support, and for community members looking for somewhere to send families when they are experiencing challenges. importantly, the services they
provide are universal, so any parent can access them. This helps to destigmatize receiving
support, and that in turn makes it more likely families will reach out when they need help.
The Prevention Councils have come up time and again in the work of the Child Safety and Family Well-Being Plan, as animportant resource for families that we not able to fully leverage right now. Parents and community partners have shared the need for more community supports and resources, opportunities for social connection, and training and
education related to mandated reporting and supporting families.
I recognize the financial constraints and scarcity mindset we are all experiencing right now.
And I would ask the committee and your colleagues in the Legislature to considerthe cost
of the investment we have made in our state's child welfare agency to intervene with families when they are in crisis and children are unsafe. There is a tremendous financial
and emotional cost to that for families and for our state. We need to invest upstream, to
support families before they are in crisis, so they can provide safety and stability for their
own children. This is better for children, and it's less costly and traumatic than an
intervention from a state agency with the power to separate children from their families.

If we care about the safety and well-being of children in Maine, we can show that by
investing in community supports for their families, and the Prevention Councils play an important role in developing and sustaining supportive communities. i urge you to support this legislation and build out the family support system in Maine.
Thankyou.

Before the Joint Standing Committee on Health and Human Services
Senator Ingwersen, esteemed members of the Health and Human Services Committee, I am
Representative Michele Meyer, serving the people of southern Maine's District 150, all of Eliot and
parts of Kittery and South Berwick. I am honored to introduce LD 1061, An Act to Increase
Community Support for Families in Maine.
As my colleagues know, child and family well-being are important issues I care deeply about. We
know that what keeps children safe is keeping families strong. One of the most important ways we can
do that is by building out a community of support for families, where parents feel they have people and places they can turn to when they face challenges. Since parenting can be difficult and hard times can fall on any family, it is critical that supportive communities are available for every family, wherever
they live in our state.
This recognition and value is reflected currently in Maine statute. The statewide network of Prevention Councils has a statutory role to review existing data to assess and monitor the extent and causes of child abuse and neglect in each county, and to carry out the following activities: coordinate services, provide training, and provide education and awareness related to the prevention of child abuse and neglect. Beyond statute, as the lead entity in each county focused on strengthening families to keep children safe, they play an important coordinating role in bringing together various partners to strengthen the overall community of support around families.
Despite their statutory role, the Prevention Councils have lacked sufficient funds to build capacity and
leverage relationships to build those strong, supportive communities we know families rely on for
social connection and access to supports and services that reduce family stress and crisis. With the
release of the long-term version of Maine's Child Safety and Family Well~Being Plan, we have a framework for how everyone can take action to keep children safe by keeping families strong. The
Prevention Councils have a clear and important role to play in this work, through supporting stigma

supporting this legislation. Thank you.

Testimony in Support of LD 1061, An Act to lncrease Community Support for Families in Maine
Provided by: Rileigh Blanchet April 4, 2025

Only allotted 3 Minutes

Senator lngwersen, Representative Meyer and members of the Joint Committee on Health and Human Services, my name is Rileigh Blanchet and l am the Social Services Director at Franklin County Children's Task Force as well as the Director for the Franklin County Prevention Council. lam also a life-long resident of Franklin County. Thank
you for the opportunity to provide testimony in support of LD 1061.

The Maine Prevention Councils provide coordinated community efforts in each county to prevent child abuse and neglect through the provision of family-strengthening programs.

Our Prevention Council is embedded and led by Franklin County Children's Task Force. Our Prevention Council was selected as one of the first demonstration sites in the state and I have been fortunate to have been involved

since the beginning.

_

What is clear to me is that community members and families need a go-to resource for support.

Families need people and places they can go to when they need help (without judgement). If I were to have any

parent with me today, they would say that the Prevention Council has been that place, and those people, for

them.

_

We support mandated reporters with training for OCFS. These in person trainings are highly sought after in our
communities.

Upstream, community-based efforts to support families are a critical (and less costly) way to strengthen families and prevent the need for downstream (child protective agency) involvement

Every community benefits from having an entity that is focused on creating community events -- these are opportunities for connection that build relationships and knowledge about resources that are available. At our
annual Children's Festival this year, we had a new dental agency attend and every parent and child that requested an appointment with them was able to get a scheduled. At our Father Daughter Dances, we saw Dads
building connections with other Dads, shaking hands, and shaking it off on the dance floor. There is one group of
three Dads who comes to the dance every year and they have an annual tradition of meeting up before the dance
to have dinner together with their daughters.

Through our Community Based Spaces work, Prevention Councils have convened community members, parents and providers alike to discuss specific community and family needs to identify opportunities in these communities. One story that always comes to mind when l mention the Community Based Spaces work happened
at our Community Dinner this fall. We had over 40 parents, providers, and children in attendance at a local
restaurant and one child looked at his mother and said, "Mom, I'm having dinner with my principal!" It gives me
goosebumps every time I remember that sweet moment.
Parents deserve places they can go to enrich their parenting free ofjudgement. We know parenting is hard. Our
parenting education programs, support groups, and play groups are a safe space for parents to make new connections, learn something they may not have considered, and provide an opportunity for their children to
play.

Support of Legislation:

LD 1061 would increase our capacity to provide universal community support for families to promote child

safety and family well-being.
Our community efforts are less costly than treatment and interventions.
We strengthen families and prevent the need for downstream child welfare involvement.
Every community benefits from having an entity that is focused on opportunities for connection that build relationships and parenting knowledge.
I would like to thank you for your time and thank you for supporting Maine's families through the Prevention
Councils.

Testimony of Erin Whitham
Regarding LD 1061: An Act to Increase Community Support for Families in Maine
Date: April 4, 2025
Senator lngwersen, Representative Meyer, and members of the Health and Human Services Committee. My name is Erin Whitham. I am the Director of Social Services at
Kennebec Valley Community Action Program in Waterville, Maine and sen/ing all of
Kennebec and Somerset Counties. The KVCAP Family Enrichment Councils in
Kennebec and Somerset are part of Maine's statewide network of Child Abuse Prevention Councils, which coordinate county-level child abuse and neglect prevention
efforts. The purpose of my testimony is to offer information about the important role
Prevention Councils play coordinating support and prevention services to families in
Maine.
Annually our Council leads a needs assessment process and develops a Prevention Plan that lays out our work for the next year with programming and supports that are responsive to our local communities' needs. ln our area, that includes facilitating and
leading parenting education, caregiver support groups, playgroups, family-friendly
community events, distribution of concrete supports, and collaboration with a wide
variety of community partners. The activities we carry out aim to strengthen protective factors among families and the community, the building blocks that help families thrive
and prevent child abuse and neglect.
Prevention Councils are small--in Kennebec and Somerset, we are fortunate to have two Community Coordinators and two Community Educators, as well as a portion of my time as Director--and yet we have a unique and important role to play in strengthening systems of support for families. Through our broad network of partners we help connect
families and providers to resources on a regular basis. Our team is knowledgeable about child development and parenting practices, and can help families troubleshoot parenting challenges or access more in depth information in the classes and workshops
we facilitate on an ongoing basis. We are also committed to helping families meet their
basic needs. A growing body of research shows that economic and concrete supports
for families prevents child abuse and strengthens families, which is why we work with
our network to distribute free diapers and wipes throughout both counties and connect families with other items, like cleaning supplies, clothing, strollers and car seats through free events like Community Baby Showers.
If you bring three people together in Kennebec and Somerset and ask them how the
community can better support families, you will have five great ideas in about five minutes. Right now, the limiting factors for our Councils are staffing and funding. State
funds make up the backbone of our program budgets, covering 90% of our personnel
costs. Both counties have been flat funded since 2018 when funds were reduced from
the previous year, while health insurance and salary expenses increase every year.
While we have been successful in expanding our work through small grants, particularly

for concrete supports, which cannot be purchased with our state funds, it is rare to find
a grant opportunity that will cover staff and operating expenses. ln Somerset, we have
one full time equivalent (FTE) for direct services for every 5,790 children in the county,
and in Kennebec, it is one FTE per 15,347. Meanwhile, in 2023 Somerset had the highest rate of child maltreatment in the state, and Kennebec the third.
Here is a simple example of the network of community support we are trying to develop
and strengthen. Last week, I took a call from a parent with a toddler referred to us by
our local WlC office. The parent had reached out for food assistance, but her family was
not eligible because they were over income. Still, between childcare, housing and utility
costs the family was struggling to make ends meet after one parent had spent a few weeks out of work recovering from an injury. Each month they were trying to make $200
stretch to cover food for a family of three, including a child on an expensive formula and transitioning to solid foods. Not only did they not have food for the weekend, they could not access food from their local foodbank because it is only open during both parents' working hours.
Fortunately, that local WlC staff person knew to connect the parent to us. We train WlC
in Mandated Reporting, and collaborate throughout the year planning community events
and referring families to one another's programs. WlC knows that right now we have a grant that allowed me to arrange a grocery store gift card for that parent, so that she
would have food for the weekend. We also arranged a time when the parent could pick
up diapers for her child and food that had been donated to us earlier in the week. After researching food resources with weekend and evening hours, I also connected the parent with Winslow Food Cupboard, a community rock star in our area, which distributes food at numerous locations at different times and days of the week.
This is child abuse prevention in action. It is parents reaching out for help, and providers partnering with them to knit supports together. Whether the ask is food or teething or isolation, Councils provide connective tissue to strengthen communities and families.
Thank you for this opportunity to share our work and the experiences of families in Kennebec and Somerset Counties.
